$comment: Bounded reviews of an exact calendar citation against pinned Bible sources. These whole-verse envelopes do not assert exact liturgical subverse cuts or authorize other citations, calendars, or source payloads. Repeated occurrences of the exact citation in the reviewed calendar reuse its review.

evidence.numberingReview: The Evangelizo HE verse labels and inspected Hebrew text match Masoretic Psalm 139. Its 14a and 14b entries each repeat the same complete verse; they are evidence for the citation, not text imported into Prosary. The USCCB appointment independently identifies Psalm 139 with the same whole-verse envelope, while marking the opening as 1b. No lectionary wording or refrain is copied.
evidence.douayRheimsBoundaryReview: The pinned DRA Psalm 138:2 contains sitting and rising; 138:3 contains the distant thoughts and the searched path; 138:4 contains the remainder of Masoretic 139:3 about all ways, followed by the opening of Masoretic 139:4. Therefore the complete-verse envelope must include DRA 138:1-4, not merely 138:1-3. DRA 138:13-14 and 138:23-24 cover the remaining appointment, retaining full verse 14. This explicit envelope takes precedence over the SIL table's nominal chapter-level 138-to-139 identity for this citation only.
evidence.otherEditionBoundaryReview: The pinned Masoretic, Synodal, Ang Dating Biblia, Crampon and Kulish passages retain the requested clauses in whole verses 1, 2, 3, 13, 14, 23 and 24. Synodal labels this Psalm 138; the other four label it Psalm 139. All six reviewed source chapters have complete numbered inventories of 24 nonempty verses. Martini has no imported Psalms; the reviewed Arabic selection has no relevant passage. Those two editions are excluded.

evidence.numberingReview: UGCC Ukraine September 2, 2026 and Royal Doors Gregorian August 26, 2026 appoint 2 Corinthians 13:3-13. The official UGCC calendar identifies Byzantine lection 197; the Greek Catholic Eparchy of Mukachevo publishes that same lection and reference, with verse 12 combining the holy kiss and greetings and verse 13 containing the Trinitarian blessing. This establishes the closing unit for these two exact calendar contexts, not for other citations or calendars.
evidence.stepBoundaryReview: Pinned STEP TVTMS lines 27448-27451 map the 13-verse ending: source 12 covers Standard 12-13 and source 13 covers Standard 14. The complete appointed closing unit therefore reaches Standard 14. All eight target source chapters were inspected: DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon, Martini and Kulish retain the blessing at 13; Ang Dating Biblia and BFBS 1905 Peshitta retain it at 14. Ordered full verses are selected without changing wording or renumbering labels. No extra source envelope or subverse notice is needed. The sparse Arabic edition has no reviewed passage and remains unavailable.

evidence.numberingReview: The original Evangelizo MAE March 8, 2026 publication has reading_code 2_Co 13,5-13. Its embedded verse markers assign the holy kiss and saints greetings to verse 12 and the complete Trinitarian blessing to verse 13. Repeated occurrences of this exact Maronite citation use the same bounded review; no other calendar is covered.
evidence.stepBoundaryReview: Pinned STEP TVTMS lines 27448-27451 map the 13-verse ending: source 12 covers Standard 12-13 and source 13 covers Standard 14. The complete appointed closing unit therefore reaches Standard 14. All eight target source chapters were inspected: DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon, Martini and Kulish retain the blessing at 13; Ang Dating Biblia and BFBS 1905 Peshitta retain it at 14. Ordered full verses are selected without changing wording or renumbering labels. No extra source envelope or subverse notice is needed. The sparse Arabic edition has no reviewed passage and remains unavailable.

evidence.numberingReview: The exact English and Latin Epistle both end after sanctifying Christ in the heart, within Bible verse 15. The full-verse corpus already retains the rest of verse 15 about readiness to explain hope; its whole-verse notice must therefore be shown even though the published reference lacks a subverse letter. The Latin source unit does not include verse 16.
evidence.editionBoundaryReview: All eight complete pinned NT sources retain the appointment within whole verses 8-15. DRA and Martini verse 16 start with modesty/fear; Ang Dating Biblia includes that clause at the end of verse 15. Preserving each existing whole verse 15 entails a wider envelope, disclosed by the notice. Do not add verse 16 merely because STEP conservatively groups 15-16 when aligning texts. No supplied Scripture wording changes. Arabic has no complete reviewed source unit.

The original Evangelizo MAE verse 13 ends with things being made visible when exposed by light. Verse 13 of all eight pinned Bible sources additionally retains the clause that everything made manifest is light. Preserve full verses 3-13 with a whole-verse notice. Verse 14 begins the awake/sleeper quotation and is outside this appointment; it is not appended.

The original Evangelizo SYE verse 18 includes John summoning two disciples after receiving their report. All eight pinned Bible sources place that summons at the beginning of verse 19, joined to sending the disciples and their question. Include complete verses 11-19 so the summons is retained, with the whole-verse notice for the additional remainder of verse 19. Do not slice or reconstruct text.

The official UGCC quotation and original Evangelizo SYE verse 19 end at Judas betraying Jesus. Royal Doors explicitly configures its reading links for RSVCE; RSVCE verse 19 also includes returning home. This shared citation therefore needs a whole-verse envelope covering both verified calendar endpoints. Ang Dating Biblia and BFBS 1905 Peshitta contain the return home at the end of verse 19; DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon, Martini and Kulish place it at the beginning of verse 20. Those six editions retain full verse 20 as well, including the crowd and inability to eat, with the whole-verse notice. The original citation stays unchanged.

The official UGCC quotation begins verse 20 with returning home. Royal Doors explicitly uses RSVCE, whose verse 20 begins with the crowd gathering, after the return home in 19. This shared citation uses a whole-verse envelope covering both verified openings. Ang Dating Biblia and BFBS 1905 Peshitta retain complete verse 19 to include returning home; DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon, Martini and Kulish already contain it in verse 20. All editions finish at verse 27. The extra Judas clause in the two expanded source verses is disclosed by the whole-verse notice; no wording or verse label is changed.

The original Evangelizo SYE verse 20 begins with Jesus coming home, then the crowd gathering. Pinned DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon, Martini and Kulish contain both clauses in verse 20. Ang Dating Biblia and BFBS 1905 Peshitta place coming home at the end of verse 19; their verse 20 begins with the crowd. Include their complete verse 19 so the opening is not lost. Every edition ends at verse 30. The whole-verse notice discloses the preceding Judas clause retained in the two expanded source verses. No verse labels or words are changed.

The original Missale Meum English and Latin Epistle ends after the sins are blotted out. Pinned DRA, Delitzsch, Synodal, Crampon and Martini verse 19 end at that clause. Ang Dating Biblia, Kulish and BFBS 1905 Peshitta verse 19 also retain the following refreshment clause. All eight existing full-verse sequences 13-15 and 17-19 therefore stay unchanged, with a whole-verse notice. Verse 20 is not added; its further material is outside the appointed ending.

The original Missale Meum English and Latin Gospel starts with Mary Magdalene, Mary of James and Salome buying spices after its liturgical incipit, omitting the Sabbath-passing opening retained in verse 1 of all eight pinned Bible sources. It ends fully at verse 7, as Jesus told the disciples. Retain full verses 1-7 and disclose the expanded opening; do not append verse 8 merely because STEP conservatively groups the neighboring verses.
